source_text:
ἐπιστήσεις δὲ αὐτοὺς καὶ ἐκ τοῦ τὸν Χριστὸν εἶναι δικαιο ύνην. ἐν μὲν οὖν τῷ
εὐεργετικῷ ἐμφαίνεται ἡ ἀγαθωσύνη, ἐν δὲ τῷ κατ' ἀξίαν ἀπονεμη τικῷ ἡ
δικαιοσύνη, ἐν δὲ τῷ ἐπιστημονικῷ τοῦ τῶν ὅλων λόγου ἡ ἀλήθεια. [v 10]
δοκιμάζοντες τί ἐστὶν εὐάρεστον τῷ Κυρίῳ. χρεία τοῦ μετὰ βουλῆς πάντα ποιεῖν, ἵνα
περισκοποῦντες ἕκαστον τῶν πρακτέων ἀπὸ ἐξετάσεως τὰ μὲν δοκιμαστὰ καὶ
εὐάρεστα τῷ Θεῷ παρα δεξώμεθα ὡς δόκιμοι τραπεζῖται, τὰ δὲ ἀδόκιμα καὶ
δυσάρεστα αὐτῷ ἀποσειώ μεθα. ἐπεὶ δὲ ἀπήρτηται τὰ τῆς φράσεως, δοκεῖ μοι οὕτως
ἂν ἀποκαταστῆναι, μὴ οὖν γίνεσθε συμμέτοχοι αὐτῶν, δοκιμάζοντες τί ἐστὶν
εὐάρεστον τῷ Κυρίῳ. εἰ καὶ ἦτέ ποτε σκότος, νῦν δὲ φῶς ὄντες ἐν Κυρίῳ ὡς τέκνα
φωτὸς περιπατεῖτε, τοὺς καρποὺς ἐπιδεικνύμενοι τοῦ φωτὸς ἐν πάσῃ ἀγαθωσύνῃ καὶ
δικαιοσύνῃ καὶ ἀληθείᾳ. [v 11a] καὶ μὴ συγκοινωνεῖτε τοῖς ἔργοις τοῖς ἀκάρποις τοῦ
σκότους. καὶ ἐν ἄλλοις τὸ μὲν τοῦ καρποῦ ὄνομα ἔταξεν ἐπὶ τοῦ πνεύματος τὸ δὲ τοῦ
ἔργου ἐπὶ τῆς σαρκός, εἰπὼν φανερὰ δέ ἐ τι τὰ ἔργα τῆ αρκό , ἅτινά ἐ τι πορνεία καὶ
τὰ ἑξῆς, ὁ δὲ καρπὸ τοῦ πνεύματό ἐ τιν ἀγάπη χαρὰ εἰρήνη καὶ τὰ ἑξῆς. νῦν
μέντοιγε τὰ τοῦ σκότους ἔργα ἄκαρπα εἶναί φησιν, οἷς κοινωνεῖ ὁ ποιῶν αὐτά. [v
11b] μᾶλλον δὲ καὶ ἐλέγχετε. ἐν ταῖς ἐντολαῖς εἶναι νομιστέον καὶ τὸ ἐλέγχειν· ὅπερ
ποιήσει ὁ μὴ ἀκουσόμενος ἄν, ὑποκριτὰ ἔκβαλε πρῶτον ἐκ τοῦ ὀφθαλμοῦ ου τὴν
δοκὸν καὶ τότε διαβλέψει ἐκβαλεῖν τὸ κάρφο ἐκ τοῦ ὀφθαλμοῦ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ ου.
διόπερ καὶ οἱ προφῆται, μηδαμῶς ἐλέγχοις ὑπεύθυνοι τυγχάνοντες, ἤλεγχον τοὺς
ἁμαρτάνοντας. [v 12] τὰ γὰρ κρυφῆ γινόμενα ὑπ' αὐτῶν αἰσχρόν ἐστι καὶ λέγειν.
τίνων αὐτῶν; οὐ πάνυ σαφῶς προεῖπεν· εἰ μὴ ἄρα τις ἀναφέρῃ ἐπὶ τοὺς υἱοὺς τῆς
ἀπειθείας τὴν λέξιν, ὥστε οὕτως αὐτὴν ἔχειν τὰ γὰρ κρυφῆ γινόμενα ὑπὸ τῶν υἱῶν
τῆς ἀπειθείας αἰσχρόν ἐστι καὶ λέγειν, ἅτινα ἦν πορνεία καὶ ἀκαθαρσία. 26 Eph. v13
[τὰ δὲ πάντα ἐλεγχόμενα ὑπὸ τοῦ φωτὸς φανεροῦνται· πᾶν γὰρ τὸ φανερούμενον
φῶς ἐστιν. διὸ λέγει, Ἔγειρε ὁ καθεύδων καὶ ἀνάστα ἐκ τῶν νεκρῶν, καὶ ἐπιφαύσει
σοι ὁ χριστός.] [Ὠριγένης δέ φησιν] ἐπείπερ τὰ ἐλεγχόμενα ἔργα τοῦ σκότους ὑπὸ
τοῦ φωτὸς φανεροῦται, μεταβαλλόντων τῶν ἐλεγχομένων εἰς φῶς, λέγεται τοῖς
καθεύδουσι καὶ ἐν νεκρότητι τυγχάνουσιν ἐκ τοῦ τὰ ἄκαρπα ἔργα τοῦ σκότους
πεποιηκέναι τὸ ἔγειρε ὁ καθεύδων καὶ ἀνάστα ἐκ τῶν νεκρῶν καὶ ἐπιφαύσει σοι ἁ
χριστός. ζητήσαι δ' ἄν τις, τίς λέγει κατὰ τὸ ἐνθάδε γεγραμμένον διὸ λέγει Ἔγειρε ὁ
καθεύδων καὶ ἀνάστα ἐκ τῶν νεκρῶν. ὁ μὲν οὖν τις φήσει ἔν τινι τῶν προφητῶν
ἀνεγνωκότα ταῦτα τὸν ἀπόστολον ἐνθάδε αὐτὸν ἀναγεγραφέναι. ἕτερος δὲ αὐτὸν
τὸν ἀπόστολον προσωποποιεῖν τινα ἐκ τοῦ πνεύματος λεγόμενα εἰς προτροπὴν τὴν
ἐπὶ μετάνοιαν. ἔτι δὲ ζητήσεις, πῶς τῷ αὐτῷ λέγεται ὡς μὲν ζῶντι καὶ καθεύδοντι
ἔγειρε ὁ καθεύδων, ὡς δὲ τεθνηκότι τὸ ἀνάστα ἐκ τῶν νεκρῶν. μήποτ' οὖν ἐπείπερ
ἔστι καὶ πνεῦμα τοῦ ἀνθρώπου τὸ ἐν αὐτῷ, ὅπερ ἐπὶ κρείττονος τετηρήκαμεν
λέγεσθαι, ἔστ
pass_a_gloss: You will also mark them from Christ's being righteousness. In the beneficent, then, goodness appears; in the distributive according to desert, justice; in the scientific of the word of all things, truth. Proving what is well-pleasing to the Lord. There is need of doing all things with counsel, so that surveying each of the things to be done from examination we may receive the approved and well-pleasing to God as approved money-changers, and shake off the unapproved and displeasing to him. And since the phrasing is incomplete, it seems to me it would be restored thus: therefore do not become fellow-partakers with them, proving what is well-pleasing to the Lord. If you were once darkness, but now being light in the Lord walk as children of light, showing the fruits of light in all goodness and righteousness and truth. And do not share with the unfruitful works of darkness. And elsewhere he ranked the name fruit upon the Spirit and the name work upon the flesh, saying now the works of the flesh are manifest, which are fornication and the rest, but the fruit of the Spirit is love joy peace and the rest. Now, however, he says the works of darkness are unfruitful, with which the one who does them shares. But rather also expose. One must suppose exposing also among the commandments; which he will do who will not hear, Hypocrite, first cast the beam out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to cast the speck out of your brother's eye. Therefore also the prophets, nowhere liable to exposures, exposed those who sinned. For the things done secretly by them it is shameful even to speak. By which them? He did not quite clearly say before; unless someone refers the wording to the sons of disobedience, so that it has thus: for the things done secretly by the sons of disobedience it is shameful even to speak, which were fornication and uncleanness. But all things exposed by the light are made manifest; for everything that is made manifest is light. Therefore it says, Awake, sleeper, and rise from the dead, and Christ will shine on you. Origen says: since the exposed works of darkness are made manifest by the light, those exposed changing into light, it is said to those sleeping and being in deadness from having done the unfruitful works of darkness, Awake, sleeper, and rise from the dead, and Christ will shine on you. One might ask who says according to what is written here Therefore it says, Awake, sleeper. One will say the apostle, having read these things in some of the prophets, wrote them here. Another will say the apostle himself personifies things said from the Spirit unto exhortation toward repentance. You will still inquire how to the same one it is said as to one living and sleeping Awake, sleeper, and as to one dead Rise from the dead. Perhaps then, since there is also a spirit of the human being that is in him, which we have observed said upon the better, and there is also something second, the soul, which is receptive of sickness and death from sins, Awake, sleeper is said because of the spirit, and Rise from the dead because of the soul; since the soul that sins, this will die, but of the spirit we nowhere found death. And Christ, being true light, will shine on the one raised from sleep and risen from the dead. Look then carefully how you walk, not as unwise but as wise, redeeming the time because the days are evil. Therefore do not become foolish, but understanding what the will of the Lord is. Origen says: the one who proves in each of the things he says and does and thinks what is well-pleasing to the Lord will also be able from much attention to look carefully how he will walk, and the one looking carefully how he will walk is altogether wise. And since some have a better intention, yet not being wise wish to look carefully how they walk, he added not as unwise but as wise; and it is a work of wisdom to look carefully also at the ethical things. Redeeming the time because the days are evil. As buying the time for themselves, it having evil days as toward human life. When therefore we spend the time on something needful, we bought it and bought it back for ourselves as sold to human wickedness; but no one living more worldly and being in cares or anxieties has bought the time for himself, but only the one spending it on something—
pass_b_english: Mark goodness, justice, and truth also from Christ's being righteousness. Goodness shows in benefaction; justice in distributing according to desert; truth in knowledge of the word of all things.

[[Ephesians 5:10 >> Bible:Ephesians 5:10]] "Proving what is well-pleasing to the Lord." Do everything with counsel. Survey each deed by examination; as approved money-changers receive what is tested and pleasing to God, and shake off what is untested and displeasing. The phrasing is incomplete; restore it thus: do not become fellow-partakers with them, proving what pleases the Lord. If you were once darkness but now are light in the Lord, walk as children of light, showing the fruit of light in all goodness, righteousness, and truth.

[[Ephesians 5:11 >> Bible:Ephesians 5:11]] "And do not share in the unfruitful works of darkness." Elsewhere he sets "fruit" on the Spirit and "work" on the flesh: "the works of the flesh are manifest… but the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace…" Here the works of darkness are unfruitful; whoever does them shares in them. "But rather also expose" belongs among the commandments—done by one who will not hear, "Hypocrite, first take the beam from your own eye." So the prophets, themselves not liable to exposure, exposed sinners.

[[Ephesians 5:12 >> Bible:Ephesians 5:12]] "For the things they do in secret it is shameful even to speak." Which "they"? He did not say clearly unless one refers it to the sons of disobedience: what they do in secret—fornication and uncleanness—is shameful even to name.

[[Ephesians 5:13–14 >> Bible:Ephesians 5:13]] "But all things exposed by the light are made plain; for everything made plain is light. Therefore it says, Awake, sleeper, and rise from the dead, and Christ will shine on you." Exposed works of darkness become plain by the light as those exposed change into light. So to sleepers deadened by unfruitful dark works it is said, "Awake… and Christ will shine on you." Who says "Therefore it says"? Some think Paul quotes a prophet; others that he personifies Spirit-speech urging repentance.

Why to the same person both "Awake, sleeper" (as living) and "Rise from the dead"? Perhaps because the human spirit in him is spoken of for the better, while the soul receives sickness and death from sins: "Awake" suits the spirit; "Rise from the dead" suits the soul—"the soul that sins will die," and we nowhere find death of the spirit. Christ, true light, shines on the one raised from sleep and risen from the dead.

[[Ephesians 5:15–17 >> Bible:Ephesians 5:15]] "Look carefully how you walk, not as unwise but as wise, redeeming the time, because the days are evil… understanding what the Lord's will is." Whoever tests each word, deed, and thought for what pleases the Lord can, by much attention, walk carefully—and such a walker is wise. Some mean well yet are not wise; so he adds "not as unwise but as wise." Wisdom watches the moral life carefully.

Redeeming the time means buying it back for yourselves while human life has evil days. Spend time on what is needed and you purchase it from sale to human wickedness. No one living for worldly cares has bought the time; only the one spending it on what is needful—continued next—buys it for the blessed life.
